summary: iter-218 / v62.3 HTTP end-to-end verification of the PAMM Strategy Execution Guard, weight pinning, material-change governance, LIVE activation enforcement, strategy-ownership endpoint, and regression. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter218_strategy_guard_http.py with 22 pytest.mark.http tests. RESULT: 21 PASSED, 1 XFAILED (documented critical bug — see 'rca of the issue'). All areas of the review request covered: (1) PATCH governance — without X-Step-Up-Bypass returns 403 step_up_required; with bypass 200 revalidation_required:true, last_validation:null, version bumped; a CERTIFIED assignment has certification_status flipped to REVALIDATION_REQUIRED and its linked cert doc in db.certifications is revoked. (2) Weight pinning — POST with target_weight 0.8 → 400 weights_fixed_in_single; PATCH min/target/max_weight each → 400; assignments store min=0.0/target=1.0/max=1.0. (3) Validation policy — fast_scalp has execution_eligibility.detail.policy='HIGH', scalper='MODERATE' (NOT nitro), sniper has NO execution_eligibility check; detail.account_scoped is a bool. (4) LIVE activation — program bound to LIVE master account (broker_environment='LIVE') → activate returns 409 certification_required; flipping account to DEMO → 200 ACTIVE. (5) Guard E2E — Scenario A LEGACY passthrough via /api/trades/manual proceeds unaffected (verified); Scenario B (STRATEGY not-ACTIVE) via HTTP is XFAILED (documented bug — PaperEngine bypasses submit_intent — see below); Scenario B via direct guard call confirms guard.authorize returns authorized=False, reason='assignment_not_active', mode='STRATEGY'; Scenario C (ACTIVE) via direct guard call returns full PAMM lineage context (pamm_program_id, assignment_id, strategy_id, strategy_version, strategy_hash, risk_profile_id, certification_id); Scenario D (max_open_positions with conservative profile + 2 seeded open trades) rejects reason='max_open_positions_reached'. (6) Strategy ownership — untagged trade on LEGACY program shows LEGACY_UNTAGGED, healthy:true; untagged trade with ACTIVE assignment shows PAMM_OWNER_UNKNOWN>=1, healthy:false, flagged classification=PAMM_OWNER_UNKNOWN; non-member user gets 403/404. (7) Regression — /api/pamm/strategies feature_flags.PAMM_REQUIRE_CERTIFICATION=true; manual trade on a plain paper account (no program pointing at it) executes with no pamm_* fields. Test runtime 6.18s. Cleanup verified post-run: 0 iter218 programs, 0 iter218 accounts, 0 iter218 users, 0 iter218 trades.

critical.issue: PaperEngine.execute() bypasses execution_authority.submit_intent — the v62.3 PAMM Strategy Execution Guard is NEVER invoked for paper-account manual trades. Only MT5BridgeEngine.execute (line 61-74) delegates to submit_intent. Since /api/trades/manual restricts to paper accounts (mode=='paper'), the entire manual path escapes the guard: a paper master-account trade with an ASSIGNED-but-not-ACTIVE strategy assignment SUCCEEDS instead of being blocked as {'blocked':'pamm_strategy_guard','reason':'assignment_not_active'}. This violates v62.3 P0 correction #1 ('PAMM Strategy Execution Guard bound inside the Execution Authority — no alternate PAMM route to MT5'): there IS an alternate route (Paper) that skips the choke point entirely. Reproduced by the xfailed test test_scenario_B_strategy_mode_not_active_blocked_HTTP. The direct-guard test test_scenario_B_direct_guard_rejects_assignment_not_active proves the guard logic itself is correct — only the wiring on PaperEngine is missing.

action_items: CRITICAL — Route PaperEngine.execute() through execution_authority.submit_intent, exactly like MT5BridgeEngine.execute() does at /app/backend/execution.py:64-74. Move the current PaperEngine.execute() body into PaperEngine.execute_authorized() (it already exists as a pattern in MT5BridgeEngine) so the guard, validation, trading authority, and intent lifecycle apply uniformly. Without this fix, any paper-master PAMM program can be traded manually with no strategy guard, no certification check, no risk-cap enforcement — completely bypassing v62.3 governance. After the fix, remove the pytest.mark.xfail from test_scenario_B_strategy_mode_not_active_blocked_HTTP and it should pass.
critical_code_review_comments: PaperEngine bypasses submit_intent (see above) — this is the only PAMM route to fills other than MT5, so the spec claim 'no alternate PAMM route to MT5' is technically true (Paper isn't MT5) but the wider invariant 'every PAMM-originated execution passes the guard' is broken for paper accounts.

modules/pamm/strategy_guard.py authorize_pamm_strategy_execution is well-structured: 13 numbered defense-in-depth checks, each surfacing a keyed check record; LEGACY early-return keeps the change zero-risk for existing programs; certification bypass via active CANARY campaign is spec-correct; strictest_limit (never averages) is used for both max_risk_per_trade and max_open_positions.

modules/pamm/strategy_assignment.py patch() correctly clears last_validation and flips certification_status to REVALIDATION_REQUIRED on a material change, and revokes the linked cert doc via certification.revoke — this is the tamper-evident chain the spec requires.

strategies/execution_eligibility.py POLICIES gives sniper=None (no gate), scalper=MODERATE, fast_scalp=HIGH, nitro_scalper=EXTREME — genuinely distinct per-strategy latency/quality thresholds, not 'nitro for everything'. validate() surfaces detail.policy and detail.account_scoped so admins can see WHY a strategy passed or failed.

modules/pamm/reconciliation/strategy_ownership.py _classify is a small, pure function — 5 distinct verdicts, LEGACY_UNTAGGED only when there's no active assignment, PAMM_OWNER_UNKNOWN as soon as one exists. Positions are FLAGGED, never guessed — the exact opposite of the failure mode this iteration is meant to prevent.

activate() correctly gates certification_required on broker_environment='LIVE' (per-account) and honours the active-CANARY exception; the message tells admins exactly which pipeline stages to run — good developer experience.

Suggestion (non-blocking): the strategy-ownership endpoint uses trade _id in flagged[].trade_id, but records use custom `trade_id` field elsewhere — small inconsistency for tooling that greps by trade_id.

Suggestion (non-blocking): patch() emits both PAMM_STRATEGY_REVALIDATION_REQUIRED AND PAMM_STRATEGY_ASSIGNED audit events on a material change. The second one is misleadingly named for a patch — consider PAMM_STRATEGY_PATCHED for clarity.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter218_strategy_guard_http.py is the canonical HTTP regression for the v62.3 strategy guard + governance surface. Key gotchas: (1) The manual-trade route (/api/trades/manual) restricts to paper-mode accounts, and PaperEngine bypasses execution_authority.submit_intent — so any Scenario B/C/D via HTTP will NOT invoke the guard until main agent routes PaperEngine through submit_intent. This test file compensates by adding *_direct variants that call authorize_pamm_strategy_execution directly with motor. Once fixed, replace the xfailed test with a real HTTP assertion and delete the *_direct variants (or keep both — the direct ones are still useful unit-style tests). (2) The paper account fixture sets broker_environment explicitly ('DEMO' or 'LIVE') AND mode='paper' — that lets us exercise the LIVE-certification-required branch while still passing the /api/trades/manual paper-mode gate. (3) All programs bound to a master account use master_account_id = str(account._id) — the guard's resolve_program queries {'master_account_id': str(account_id), 'status': {'$nin': ['archived','closed']}}. Newly-created programs have status='active' so they match. (4) The PATCH-cert-revoke test injects a fake pamm_strategy cert doc (kind='pamm_strategy', subject=program_id, revoked:false, status:'ACTIVE', expires_at in +90 days), stamps assignment.certification_status=CERTIFIED + cert_id, then PATCHes risk_profile — main agent's patch() calls certification.revoke() which flips {status:'REVOKED', revoked:true, revoked_at:...}. Our assertion is tolerant to either the revoked bool or the status string. (5) The suite runs in ~6 seconds and cleans up all its side effects; no need to reset any global state between iterations.
rca of the issue: PaperEngine.execute() bypasses execution_authority.submit_intent, so the v62.3 PAMM Strategy Execution Guard is not invoked for paper-account manual trades. Reproduction: (a) create a PAMM program, (b) create a paper account owned by admin (mode='paper', broker_environment='DEMO'), (c) set program.master_account_id = str(account._id), (d) POST /api/pamm/programs/{pid}/strategy assigning sniper (status=ASSIGNED, NOT activated), (e) POST /api/trades/manual for that account_id → the trade SUCCEEDS (returns a trade doc) instead of returning {'blocked':'pamm_strategy_guard','reason':'assignment_not_active'}. Verified with test_scenario_B_strategy_mode_not_active_blocked_HTTP (xfails as expected). The guard logic itself is correct — test_scenario_B_direct_guard_rejects_assignment_not_active calls authorize_pamm_strategy_execution() directly against the same DB state and gets the correct rejection. Mitigation: rewrite PaperEngine.execute() to delegate to submit_intent exactly as MT5BridgeEngine.execute() does (5-line change): body becomes 'from execution_authority import submit_intent; return await submit_intent(user_id=..., account=..., signal=..., engine=self, max_concurrent=..., cfg_account_id=...)', and the current body moves into PaperEngine.execute_authorized(self, *, user_id, account, signal, max_concurrent=0, cfg_account_id=None, intent=None, authorization=None) with the standard capability-verification prelude from MT5BridgeEngine.execute_authorized (lines 84-93). After the fix, all paper-master PAMM trades will be governed by the strategy guard, certification checks, risk-cap enforcement, and the canonical intent lifecycle — matching the review request's stated behaviour.
